questions.subject: physics
questions.content: If energy ($E$), velocity ($V$) and time ($T$) are chosen as the fundamental quantities, the dimensional formula of surface tension will be:

solution.text:
Surface tension ($S$) is force per unit length or energy per unit area. So, $[S] = [M L^0 T^{-2}]$. Let $S \propto E^a V^b T^c$. Then $[M L^0 T^{-2}] = [M L^2 T^{-2}]^a [L T^{-1}]^b [T]^c$. Equating powers of $M, L, T$:
$a = 1$
$2a + b = 0 \implies b = -2$
$-2a - b + c = -2 \implies -2(1) - (-2) + c = -2 \implies c = -2$.
Thus, $[S] = [E V^{-2} T^{-2}]$.

questions.subject: physics
questions.content: A physical quantity $P$ is described by the relation $P = a^{1/2} b^2 c^3 d^{-4}$. If the relative errors in the measurement of $a, b, c$ and $d$ respectively, are $2\%, 1\%, 3\%$ and $5\%$, then the relative error in $P$ will be:

solution.text: The maximum percentage error is given by: $\frac{\Delta P}{P} \times 100 = \frac{1}{2}\frac{\Delta a}{a} \times 100 + 2\frac{\Delta b}{b} \times 100 + 3\frac{\Delta c}{c} \times 100 + 4\frac{\Delta d}{d} \times 100$. Substituting the values: $\frac{\Delta P}{P} \times 100 = \frac{1}{2}(2\%) + 2(1\%) + 3(3\%) + 4(5\%) = 1\% + 2\% + 9\% + 20\% = 32\%$.

questions.subject: physics
questions.content: Two particles $A$ and $B$ are projected simultaneously in the direction of the horizontal and the vertical respectively from the same point, with speeds $u$ and $v$. The shortest distance between them is:

options.text: They will never be at a minimum distance other than $0$

solution.text: Since they are both in free fall, their relative acceleration is zero. Therefore, their relative velocity is constant. The initial relative velocity of $B$ with respect to $A$ is $\vec{v}_{BA} = v\hat{j} - u\hat{i}$. The relative path is a straight line. Since they start from the same point, the relative path passes through the origin. Therefore, the shortest distance between them is $0$ at $t=0$, and they continuously separate.

questions.subject: physics
questions.content: A particle is projected horizontally with a speed $u$ from the top of a plane inclined at an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal. How far from the point of projection will the particle strike the plane?

solution.text: Let the point of projection be the origin. The equation of the trajectory is $y = -\frac{gx^2}{2u^2}$. The equation of the inclined plane is $y = -x \tan\theta$. Finding the intersection: $-x \tan\theta = -\frac{gx^2}{2u^2} \implies x = \frac{2u^2 \tan\theta}{g}$. The distance along the incline is $s = x \sec\theta = \frac{2u^2 \tan\theta \sec\theta}{g}$.

questions.subject: physics
questions.content: A system consists of two identical blocks, each of mass $m$, connected by a light spring of stiffness $k$, resting on a smooth horizontal surface. A constant horizontal force $F$ is applied to one of the blocks. What is the maximum extension of the spring during the subsequent motion?

solution.text: Let us use the center of mass frame. The acceleration of the CM is $a_{cm} = \frac{F}{2m}$. In the CM frame, a pseudo force $-\frac{F}{2}$ acts on both blocks. The block where $F$ is applied experiences a net force $F - \frac{F}{2} = \frac{F}{2}$ away from the CM, while the other block experiences a pseudo force $\frac{F}{2}$ also away from the CM. The work done by these pseudo forces in the CM frame until maximum extension $x_{max}$ (where both blocks come to rest in CM frame) is $\frac{F}{2} \frac{x_{max}}{2} + \frac{F}{2} \frac{x_{max}}{2} = \frac{F}{2} x_{max}$. Equating this work to the potential energy of the spring $\frac{1}{2} k x_{max}^2$, we get $\frac{F}{2} x_{max} = \frac{1}{2} k x_{max}^2 \implies x_{max} = \frac{F}{k}$.

questions.subject: physics
questions.content: A block of mass 10 kg is placed on a rough horizontal surface having coefficient of friction $\mu = 0.5$. If a horizontal force of 100 N is acting on it, then the acceleration of the block will be ($g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2$):

solution.text: Normal reaction $N = mg = 10 \times 10 = 100$ N. Maximum friction $f_{max} = \mu N = 0.5 \times 100 = 50$ N. The applied force is $F = 100$ N. Since $F > f_{max}$, the block moves. Net force $= F - f_{max} = 100 - 50 = 50$ N. Acceleration $a = \frac{F_{net}}{m} = \frac{50}{10} = 5 \text{ m/s}^2$.

questions.subject: physics
questions.content: A body of mass $m$ starts from rest and is subjected to a force $F = cx$ where $c$ is a constant and $x$ is the distance. The work done by the force in moving the body a distance $d$ is:

solution.text: Work done $W = \int_{0}^{d} F dx = \int_{0}^{d} (cx) dx = c \left[\frac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^d = \frac{1}{2}cd^2$.

questions.subject: physics
questions.content: A child is standing with folded hands at the center of a platform rotating about its central axis. The kinetic energy of the system is $K$. The child now stretches his arms so that the moment of inertia of the system doubles. The kinetic energy of the system now is:

solution.text: Since no external torque acts on the system, angular momentum $L$ is conserved. Kinetic energy $K = \frac{L^2}{2I}$. If the moment of inertia becomes $2I$, the new kinetic energy $K' = \frac{L^2}{2(2I)} = \frac{1}{2} \frac{L^2}{2I} = \frac{K}{2}$.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.content:
If $20.0 \text{ g}$ of $\text{CaCO}_3$ is treated with $20.0 \text{ g}$ of $\text{HCl}$, how many grams of $\text{CO}_2$ can be generated according to the following reaction? (Molar mass: $\text{CaCO}_3 = 100$, $\text{HCl} = 36.5$, $\text{CO}_2 = 44$) 
 $\text{CaCO}_3(s) + 2\text{HCl}(aq) \rightarrow \text{CaCl}_2(aq) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(l) + \text{CO}_2(g)$

solution.text: Moles of $\text{CaCO}_3 = \frac{20.0}{100} = 0.20 \text{ mol}$. Moles of $\text{HCl} = \frac{20.0}{36.5} = 0.548 \text{ mol}$. From the stoichiometry, 1 mole of $\text{CaCO}_3$ requires 2 moles of $\text{HCl}$. Therefore, 0.20 mole of $\text{CaCO}_3$ requires $0.20 \times 2 = 0.40 \text{ mol}$ of $\text{HCl}$. Since we have 0.548 mol of HCl, $\text{CaCO}_3$ is the limiting reagent. Moles of $\text{CO}_2$ produced = Moles of $\text{CaCO}_3$ consumed = $0.20 \text{ mol}$. Mass of $\text{CO}_2 = 0.20 \times 44 = 8.80 \text{ g}$.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.content: The ratio of the radius of the second orbit of $\text{Li}^{2+}$ to the radius of the third orbit of $\text{He}^{+}$ is:

solution.text: The radius of the $n^{\text{th}}$ Bohr orbit is given by $r \propto \frac{n^2}{Z}$. For $\text{Li}^{2+}$, $n = 2$ and $Z = 3$. Therefore, $r_{\text{Li}^{2+}} \propto \frac{2^2}{3} = \frac{4}{3}$. For $\text{He}^{+}$, $n = 3$ and $Z = 2$. Therefore, $r_{\text{He}^{+}} \propto \frac{3^2}{2} = \frac{9}{2}$. The ratio is $\frac{4/3}{9/2} = \frac{4}{3} \times \frac{2}{9} = \frac{8}{27}$.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.content: Which of the following carbocations is most stable?

solution.text: Tropylium cation is a 7-membered ring with 6 $\pi$ electrons in complete conjugation. It satisfies Huckel's rule ($4n+2 \pi$ electrons, where $n=1$) and is therefore aromatic. Aromatic carbocations are exceptionally stable, often more stable than even triphenylmethyl cation in certain conditions, but generally Tropylium is considered highly stable due to aromaticity.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.content: Arrange the following in increasing order of acidic strength: (I) Phenol (II) p-Nitrophenol (III) m-Nitrophenol (IV) p-Cresol

solution.text: Acidic strength depends on the stability of the phenoxide ion. Electron Withdrawing Groups (EWG) like $-\text{NO}_2$ increase stability (and thus acidity) via $-R$ and $-I$ effects. The $-R$ effect of $-\text{NO}_2$ is highly stabilizing at the para position, making p-nitrophenol the most acidic. m-Nitrophenol experiences only the $-I$ effect, so it's less acidic than p-nitrophenol but more acidic than phenol. Electron Donating Groups (EDG) like $-\text{CH}_3$ decrease acidity via $+I$ and hyperconjugation. Thus p-cresol is the least acidic. Order: IV < I < III < II.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.content: How many total structural isomers are possible for the molecular formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{14}$?

solution.text:
The structural isomers of hexane ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{14}$) are:
1. n-hexane
2. 2-methylpentane
3. 3-methylpentane
4. 2,2-dimethylbutane
5. 2,3-dimethylbutane
There are exactly 5 structural isomers.

questions.subject: maths
questions.content: Let $R$ be a relation on the set $N$ of natural numbers defined by $n R m$ if $n$ divides $m$. Then $R$ is:

solution.text:
For any $n \in N$, $n$ divides $n$, so $R$ is reflexive.
If $n$ divides $m$ and $m$ divides $p$, then $n$ divides $p$. So $R$ is transitive.
If $2$ divides $4$, it is not true that $4$ divides $2$. So $R$ is not symmetric.
Hence, $R$ is reflexive and transitive but not symmetric.

questions.subject: maths
questions.content: If $|z - 1| + |z + 1| = 2$, then the locus of $z$ in the complex plane is:

solution.text: The equation $|z - z_1| + |z - z_2| = 2a$ represents an ellipse if $2a > |z_1 - z_2|$. If $2a = |z_1 - z_2|$, it represents the line segment joining $z_1$ and $z_2$. Here, $z_1 = 1, z_2 = -1$. The distance is $|1 - (-1)| = 2$. Since the given sum is exactly $2$, the locus is the straight line segment joining $1$ and $-1$ on the real axis.

questions.subject: maths
questions.content: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of the equation $x^2 - x + 1 = 0$, then $\alpha^{2009} + \beta^{2009} = $

solution.text:
The roots of $x^2 - x + 1 = 0$ are $-\omega$ and $-\omega^2$, where $\omega$ is a complex cube root of unity.
So, $\alpha = -\omega$ and $\beta = -\omega^2$.
$\alpha^{2009} + \beta^{2009} = (-\omega)^{2009} + (-\omega^2)^{2009} = -(\omega^{2009} + \omega^{4018})$.
Since $2009 = 3 \times 669 + 2$, $\omega^{2009} = \omega^2$.
And $4018 = 3 \times 1339 + 1$, $\omega^{4018} = \omega^1$.
Therefore, $\alpha^{2009} + \beta^{2009} = -(\omega^2 + \omega)$.
Since $1 + \omega + \omega^2 = 0$, $\omega + \omega^2 = -1$.
So, $\alpha^{2009} + \beta^{2009} = -(-1) = 1$.

questions.subject: maths
questions.content: Evaluate the integral $I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \frac{\sin^3 x}{\sin^3 x + \cos^3 x} dx$.

solution.text: Using the property $\int_0^a f(x) dx = \int_0^a f(a - x) dx$, we have $I = \int_0^{\pi/2} \frac{\sin^3(\pi/2 - x)}{\sin^3(\pi/2 - x) + \cos^3(\pi/2 - x)} dx = \int_0^{\pi/2} \frac{\cos^3 x}{\cos^3 x + \sin^3 x} dx$. Adding the two expressions for $I$, we get $2I = \int_0^{\pi/2} \frac{\sin^3 x + \cos^3 x}{\sin^3 x + \cos^3 x} dx = \int_0^{\pi/2} 1 dx = \frac{\pi}{2}$. Therefore, $I = \frac{\pi}{4}$.
